paragraphs: See Yerushalmi Chagigah, chapter 2, halakhah 2: the incident with his daughter.

notes.text: The heading עלי בצלים literally reads “onion leaves.” How it functions as a designation in the account of “his daughter” remains unclear.

The saved named Guggenheimer Chagigah 2:2 narrative explicitly names Miriam daughter of Alei Betzalim (מרים ברת עלי בצלים). This identifies the daughter in the cited narrative and shows the heading functioning as her father’s designation, qualifying the earlier note’s lack of context. The literal “onion leaves” reading does not establish a modern identity or etymology; no extra narrative is inserted into the source body.

Hyman’s printed notice (vol. III, p. 983) points to the incident with his daughter. In Yerushalmi Chagigah 2:2, the pious man sees Miriam, daughter of Alei Betzalim, in a vision. The text gives two accounts of her punishment. The narrative supplies her name and her father’s designation while leaving the origin of that designation open.
